178755714.title: File:Feeds, Feelings, and Focus - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Examining the Cognitive and Mental Health Correlates of Short-Form Video Use.pdf

ImageDescription.value: The resurgence of short-form videos (SFVs), popularized by TikTok and Douyin, has transformed social media platforms, with features like Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts fostering their widespread adoption. Although initially geared toward entertainment, SFVs are increasingly used in education, political campaigns, advertising, and consumerism, yet their design, characterized by endless scrolling interfaces, has raised concerns about addiction and negative health implications. Given the recent surge of studies on SFV apps, a comprehensive synthesis is needed to clarify how SFV use relates to different health indicators. This systematic review and meta-analytic investigation comprised data from 98,299 participants across 71 studies. Increased SFV use was associated with poorer cognition (moderate mean effect size, <var>r</var> = −.34), with attention (<var>r</var> = −.38) and inhibitory control (<var>r</var> = −.41) yielding the strongest associations. Similarly, increased SFV use was associated with poorer mental health (weak mean effect size, <var>r</var> = −.21), with stress (<var>r</var> = −.34) and anxiety (<var>r</var> = −.33) showing the strongest associations. These findings were consistent across youth and adult samples and across different SFV platforms. Relatively few studies examined cognitive domains beyond attention and inhibitory control (e.g., memory, reasoning), highlighting critical directions for future research. Interestingly, SFV use was not associated with body image or self-esteem, which may reflect the diverse content and creators featured on these platforms. Further research is therefore needed to clarify how different types of content exposure may shape these associations. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of understanding the broader health implications of SFV use, given its pervasive role in daily life and potential to impact health, behavior, and well-being. By synthesizing current evidence, this study provides a critical foundation for future research to explore understudied health domains (e.g., cognitive health, physical health) and offers insights to guide public discourse and the development of research-informed approaches for promoting more balanced engagement with SFVs.

Artist.value: Lan Nguyen, Jared Walters, Siddharth Paul, Shay Monreal Ijurco, Georgia E. Rainey, Nupur Parekh, Gabriel Blair, Miranda Darrah

197927126.title: File:TikTok Overnight Challenge Ends in Arrest After Cops Find Livestream.webm

ImageDescription.value:
On January 13, 2026, deputies responded to a Walmart following a reported burglary involving a man allegedly livestreaming on TikTok as part of a 24-hour overnight challenge.

Dispatch advised deputies that a male was reportedly hiding inside the store and livestreaming from the dog bed section. When deputies arrived, Walmart staff said they were unaware that anyone remained inside the store. Deputies entered through a side grocery entrance and searched the area described by the caller.

Deputies located a man hiding between dog beds while actively recording on his phone. He was instructed to come out of the aisle and was placed in handcuffs while deputies investigated the situation.

The store manager agreed to pursue charges and requested that the man be issued a trespass warning from the property. After being read his Miranda Rights, which he said he understood, the man told deputies he believed he could make money from TikTok views and had decided to attempt a 24-hour challenge inside Walmart. He also admitted to taking an iPhone charger.

The man was arrested and charged with petit theft and burglary of an occupied structure.

This body camera footage captures the law enforcement response, investigation, apprehension of the suspect, and the events that led to the arrest.
